initialize.instructions: Write tools end with a receipt: `[seq N]` means committed; `(export pending: …)` means committed with only the file export queued; `No change … already …` without a seq means the value was already stored. On a native store the database is the authority: a hand edit to a .taskmaster/ file takes effect only after backlog_sync(). backlog_store_status shows dirty or quarantined files. JSON results carry the same receipt as "seq" and "export_pending" fields; a result starting "Error:" with no seq wrote nothing.

tools.description:
Where the project stands: progress per epic, in-progress tasks, blocked items, next priorities, and stats.
Open lines of work with their next steps are on `backlog_thread_list`, not here.

verbose.description:
If True, include archived task count in stats and show up to
10 stale tasks and all next-up items. Default (slim) mode omits
archived counts, caps next-up at 5, and caps stale tasks at 3.

tools.name: backlog_status

tools.description:
Which tasks match: by epic, status, priority, phase, area or waiting on a
person, one line each, active tasks first, capped at `limit` with an
overflow footer. A row shows `waiting-on-human:` when the task has a
human_action.

area.description:
Filter by area ID: tasks tagged with it, and the untagged tasks
of epics filed under it.

priority.description: Filter by priority: critical, high, medium, low

status.description: Filter by status: todo, in-progress, in-review, done, blocked

verbose.description:
If True, include heavy fields (notes) per task entry. Slim
(default) shows id, title, tldr, priority, epic, and status only.

waiting_on_human.description:
Only tasks with a human_action set — what waits on
someone to act or decide.

tools.name: backlog_list_tasks

tools.description:
Get details for a single task including epic context and related tasks.
For what blocks it or whether it can close now, `backlog_context(focus=<id>,
scope="task")` answers in one call.

Slim (tldr, status, priority, key links) by default; verbose adds the body fields, sections
picks named sections, expand_links adds tldrs to linked ids.

expand_links.description:
If True, replace bare IDs in depends_on,
related_issues with {id, tldr} pills.

provenance.description:
With sections, annotate each section with where its text came
from — an imported document (path, content_hash, imported_seq), an
inline field, or a file read off disk that was never imported.

sections.description:
Named sections to include (e.g. ["notes", "spec"]).
Canonical sections for tasks: notes, review_instructions, spec,
plan, design, analysis, roadmap.

verbose.description:
If True, include full body fields (notes, review_instructions,
docs, spec-review, epic context, recently completed tasks).

tools.name: backlog_get_task

tools.description:
Read one entity's prose — named sections, or the whole document body.

The kind-general companion to `backlog_get_task(sections=...)`: use it to read
a handover's decisions, an issue's repro steps or an epic's design without
pulling the entity's whole record. On a native store the text comes from the
store itself; a task `docs` file that has never been imported is read from
disk and `provenance=True` says so.

provenance.description: Annotate each section with where its text came from.

sections.description:
Named sections to return (e.g. ["decisions", "blockers"]).
Omit for the whole document body. Canonical sections per kind:
task — notes, review_instructions, spec, plan, design, analysis,
roadmap; handover — decisions, notes, blockers, where_id_start;
issue — repro, investigation, notes; epic — notes, design, spec,
roadmap, analysis; phase — notes, design, roadmap. Other kinds have
no named sections.

tools.name: backlog_document

tools.description:
Import a task's external documents into the store, so reads stop touching files.

Explicit and caller-initiated: nothing watches the files and nothing imports on
read. Each named section's file is read once, stored with its content hash, and
served from the store from then on — including after the file changes on disk, so
re-run this when a document is edited. Re-importing unchanged prose does nothing.

With `content`, the text you pass is imported instead and no file is read: use it
when the file is on your machine, not the server's (a team server). The task must
already declare each section's path. An uploaded document is stored on the team
server; a restore of the server keeps it only through the server's state backup
(team-server-013), so commit the file to the code repository if it must outlive
both. Send large documents one section per call (the server caps a request's size).

content.description: Section name to that document's text, e.g. `{"spec": "# Spec\n..."}`.

entity_id.description: The task ID whose documents to import.

expected_hash.description:
Section name to the sha256 `content_hash` you expect the store to
hold now ("" for none), from `backlog_document(provenance=True)`; a section
whose stored copy differs is not imported. Pass it when several people import
the same task's documents.

kind.description: Only "task" — task `docs` paths are the external documents the store serves.

sections.description:
Document sections to import (spec, plan, design, analysis, roadmap).
Omit to import every document the task declares. Not with `content`.

tools.name: backlog_document_import

tools.description:
Report the state of the store's derived tables (FTS, paths, links, related).

They live in `.taskmaster/local/store.db` beside the authoritative rows and are
refreshed inside the transaction of every tool call; `rebuild` recomputes them
from the entity rows should they ever drift.

rebuild.description:
Recompute every derived table from the entity rows before reporting.
The authoritative tables are not touched and no file is re-read. On a
native store this is the graph repair and covers only `entity_paths`,
`links`, `handover_tasks` and `related` (not search): they are compared
with the full oracle and only the differing rows are replaced, in one
transaction.

verify.description:
On a native store, compare the graph tables with the full oracle
and report the differences and the cost, changing nothing. A legacy
store has no such verifier: it reports the row counts and says that
nothing was compared, and does not rebuild.

tools.name: backlog_index_status

tools.description:
Report the state of the SQLite store (`.taskmaster/local/store.db`).

The store is the authority: root and how it was resolved, schema version,
database and WAL size, the last 20 changes, dirty and quarantined
projection files, live sessions, any filesystem warning, merge conflicts in
the last 24 hours, databases an earlier recovery moved aside, and the
pending Linear push count.

Read-only: a missing or damaged store is reported on the `Warning:` line,
not created or moved aside.

deep.description:
Run the full `integrity_check` now (seconds on a large store) instead of showing the stored result of
the one-time check. On a team server only the operator may; members see the stored line.

tools.name: backlog_store_status

tools.description:
List, compare or resolve files flagged because they and the store both changed.

A file is flagged when it and the store both changed: nothing is merged,
the file is left as written, and exports to it pause until it is resolved.
Every tool result names flagged files until then.

- no `file`: list flagged files.
- `file` only: show both versions -- the file as last seen and as on disk
  now, and the exact text the store would write.
- `file` and `take="file"`: import the file as it is on disk now; the
  store's replaced values stay in the change log.
- `file` and `take="store"`: write the store's version over the file (or
  move/remove it if the entity is archived or deleted); the replaced file
  text is kept in the resolution's change row.

A resolution always takes one whole file. For `backlog.yaml` that means
every epic and phase entry in it at once: there is no per-entity choice, so
compare the two versions first and edit the side you keep if it needs
pieces of the other.

file.description:
Flagged file path relative to `.taskmaster/` (e.g. `tasks/core-001.md`, `backlog.yaml`).
Empty lists the flagged files.

take.description:
`"file"` keeps the file as it is on disk; `"store"` writes the store's version over it.
Empty with `file` set shows both versions without changing anything.

tools.name: backlog_resolve_conflict

tools.description:
Import hand edits to `.taskmaster/` files into a native store.

A native store never re-reads its projection files on its own, so a hand edit
to a task, epic, handover, `backlog.yaml` or `project.yaml` takes effect only
after this call.

No arguments syncs every file; `files` syncs only those; `sync_id` checks on a
sync an earlier call started. Each call returns within ~15 s with "Sync running"
(call again with the sync_id), "Sync complete" with counts, or the conflicts and
quarantined files to settle with `backlog_resolve_conflict`. On a legacy store
it does nothing (hand edits import on every call). On a team server only the host
operator can run it.

files.description:
Paths relative to `.taskmaster/` to sync, e.g. `["tasks/core-001.md"]`
(a leading `.taskmaster/` is accepted). Omit to sync every file.

sync_id.description:
The id from a "Sync running" answer. A finished sync returns its stored
result; edits made after it need a fresh `backlog_sync()`.

tools.name: backlog_sync

tools.description:
Read-only SQL over the backlog store (.taskmaster/local/store.db). Use it to dig deeper
than the one-line edit hook: closed history for a path, titles, related entities, FTS.

sql.description:
one SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT, recursive CTEs allowed). Writes, PRAGMA, ATTACH and
multiple statements are rejected, as is a forbidden keyword inside a double-quoted
identifier — quote string values with single quotes. Queries are cut off after 5 s.

tools.name: backlog_query

tools.description:
What the backlog holds on a topic: full-text search across tasks, epics, bugs, issues,
handovers, decisions and ideas, ranked by relevance (bm25); a hit in the prose alone shows the
matching text. No date filter: `backlog_handover_list` filters handovers by date, thread, task
or status, and `backlog_thread_resume` answers where a line of work left off.

kinds.description:
Optional filter, e.g. ["bug", "issue"]. Unknown kinds are ignored; omit for all.
Valid kinds: task, epic, bug, issue, handover, decision, idea.

query.description:
Search text (case-insensitive). Matched against titles and bodies (notes,
descriptions, evidence, handover prose). Multiple words are ANDed together.

tools.name: backlog_search

tools.description: Show the full dependency chain for a task — what it depends on (upstream) and what it unblocks (downstream).

depth.description:
How many hops to follow each way: a strict integer from 1 to 10
(a boolean, string or float is refused, never coerced). Default 1: direct
dependencies and dependents only, exactly as before. Above 1, a
transitive section per direction follows the one-hop answer, listing
each task at its shortest distance (2..depth) with the task it was
reached through. Archived tasks are followed; deleted ids upstream show
as missing and are not followed; an unreadable `depends_on` is named,
not followed. Cycles are reported, never looped. At most 200 tasks are
listed per direction (the rest are counted as truncated), and the
traversal stops after 5 s, saying so.

tools.name: backlog_dependencies
backlog_next_available

tools.description:
Check backlog integrity: dangling dependency refs, missing dates on done tasks,
docs paths that don't exist on disk, circular deps, and status inconsistencies.
tools.name: backlog_validate

tools.description:
Initialize taskmaster in the current project on the native store.

Creates `.taskmaster/` with `taskmaster.json`, `backlog.yaml` and the `tasks/`, `areas/`,
`handovers/` and `issues/` directories (all meant to be committed), plus the machine-local
`.taskmaster/local/` (store.db, PROGRESS.md, caches; it carries its own .gitignore). The
store is created as a native authority, so every later call is served natively. Refuses
when the project already has a backlog or a store, and in a linked worktree or submodule;
run again, it finishes an init that was interrupted before its store was activated.

legacy_store.description:
True opts out of the native store and creates the legacy SQLite store
      instead, for a host that cannot run the native coordinator service. It is
      recorded in taskmaster.json, and the operator cutover can convert it later.

location.description: Only "tracked" is accepted (files always go in `.taskmaster/`); kept for compatibility.

project_name.description: Name for the project. Defaults to the directory name.

schema_version.description:
Leave at 0, which picks the current schema. 2 and 3 are legacy schemas
      kept for migration tooling; they write files only and never a native store.

tools.name: backlog_init

tools.description:
Adopt this project's backlog into the SQLite store.

The store adopts whatever schema it finds when it first opens the project,
so there is no file-rewrite step: this moves a legacy `.claude/` or root
layout into `.taskmaster/` and opens the store. Running it on an adopted
project just reports the counts.
tools.name: backlog_migrate_v3

tools.description: Alias of backlog_migrate_v3.
tools.name: backlog_migrate_v4

tools.description:
One-time optional migration: assign a `lane` (by priority) to every task that
lacks one. For tasks already in-progress/in-review/done, mark their lane's required
gates skipped(reason="grandfathered") so enforcement never retroactively wedges
in-flight work. Tasks that already have a lane are left untouched.

grandfather_active.description: if true, grandfather gates on non-todo tasks (recommended).

tools.name: backlog_backfill_lanes

tools.description:
Migrate the v3 backlog from `.claude/` or root layout into canonical `.taskmaster/`.

Moves backlog.yaml + the artifact subdirs (tasks, handovers, issues,
auto, PROGRESS.md, viewer.json) into `.taskmaster/`.
Idempotent: re-running on a canonical layout is a no-op. Refuses to clobber:
if a destination file already holds different content, nothing moves and the
conflicts are reported. After a successful `.claude/` migration, the redundant
`.claude/taskmaster.json` config is deleted.

dry_run.description: When true, returns the move plan without modifying anything.

tools.name: backlog_canonicalize_layout

tools.description:
Write a session handover so a later session can resume: decisions, blockers, where to
start next. `body` is freeform markdown (Decisions / Blockers / Where I'd start / Open threads).

A line of work keeps one open resume point: older open handovers in the same thread are
superseded automatically and listed in the result as "Auto-superseded". With a derived
thread (no `thread` given), only open handovers that share a task id, or that both name
no task, are superseded.

flag_for_review.description: When True, flags this handover for retro extraction.

options.description:
Rarely-set fields — branch, tip_commit (frontmatter git
context), context_size_at_write (compaction marker), review_reason
(used only when flag_for_review).

session_kind.description:
`continuity` for a normal wrap-up, `deep-context` (long session, lots to
carry over) or `milestone`. `auto-stage` (bookkeeping checkpoint, born closed) and
`task-complete` (short wrap-up) also exist. The default `end-of-day` is accepted as `continuity`.

supersedes.description:
Optional id of an older handover this one supersedes; the old
one gets a `superseded_by:` field and a SUPERSEDED callout. Only
needed across threads — within a thread it is automatic.

task_ids.description: Tasks this handover relates to (surfaces in pick-task).

thread.description: Thread this handover belongs to (stable resume token). Auto-derived from bundle/epic/task/tldr when empty.

tools.name: backlog_handover_create

tools.description:
Which handovers exist, newest first, filtered by date, thread, task or
status. No topic search: `backlog_search` matches text, and
`backlog_thread_resume` answers where a line of work left off. Text
one-liners by default; `format="json"` for a parseable envelope.

Searches the handover index — the most recent 30. Older handovers are
archived, not deleted: when any exist the answer says how many went
unsearched, and `include_archived=True` searches them too.

format.description:
"text" (default) or "json". JSON returns {"handovers": [...],
"returned", "total", "truncated", "archived_omitted"}. Every
handover has the same keys, empty when absent: id, date, created,
thread, session_kind, status, tldr, next_action, task_ids,
tip_commit, branch, links ([{"type", "target"}], supersession
included), superseded_by. `total` counts matches before `limit`;
`archived_omitted` counts archived handovers not searched;
`truncated` is true when either left something out. Errors are
{"error": "..."}. `server` names the taskmaster that answered: mode
(local, per-session or team), project, version, and for per-session
the reason and whether the local server was opted out of.

include_archived.description:
Also search and list the archived handovers beyond
the 30-entry index.

latest_per_thread.description:
Only the newest open handover of each thread, among
those the other filters match. A handover with no thread is its
own group.

limit.description:
Max entries returned (default 50 — above the 30-entry index, so
by default it only cuts with include_archived). 0 = no cap.

session_kind.description:
If set, only entries with this session_kind
(e.g. "continuity", "deep-context", "milestone").

since.description:
YYYY-MM-DD, exactly that form. Only entries dated on or after
it. Anything else is refused with an error.

status.description: One of open, closed, superseded, or "all" (default).

task_id.description: If set, only entries whose `task_ids` list contains this id.

thread.description:
If set, only entries in this thread (its name as
`backlog_thread_list` shows it).

until.description:
YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only entries dated on or before it;
since=until=one day returns just that day.

verbose.description:
Text only. Adds next_action, task_ids, status, thread, branch,
tip_commit and links per entry. Slim (default) shows id, date,
kind and tldr.

tools.name: backlog_handover_list

tools.description:
Read handover <id>: slim frontmatter by default; verbose adds the body, sections picks named
sections (decisions, notes, blockers, where_id_start), expand_links adds tldrs to linked ids.

handover_id.description: The handover id, as shown by a list or search.

sections.description: Named body sections to return instead of the slim view.

tools.name: backlog_handover_get

tools.description:
Import hand edits to handover files (a handover-only `backlog_sync`) and rebuild the 30-entry handover index.

On a team server only the host operator can run it.
tools.name: backlog_handover_resync

tools.description:
What is still open, per line of work (thread / workstream): each open or
parked thread with its newest open handover's summary, next step and tasks.
Resume one with `backlog_thread_resume(<name>)`.

include_archived.description:
Also list threads whose handovers are all outside the
30-entry handover index; by default they are only counted.

tools.name: backlog_thread_list

tools.description:
Where a line of work left off: its thread's newest open handover (its
newest when none is open) in full, frontmatter + body, in one call. A miss
answers the closest thread names.

ref.description: A thread name, or any handover id in the thread (however stale).

tools.name: backlog_thread_resume

tools.description: Set a thread's status. Writing a new handover into the thread later reopens it.

name.description: The thread name, as shown by `backlog_thread_list()`.

reason.description: Optional note on why; stored with the status.

tools.name: backlog_thread_update

tools.description:
Link two entities of any kind — tasks, bugs, issues, decisions, ideas,
notes, handovers — and read the links back. The server writes the inverse
side automatically and rejects unknown ids, invalid types and kind
mismatches; `query(source=X)` lists X's links, inverses and the links its
fields derive (a task's depends_on) included. A dependency between two tasks
is not a link: set it with backlog_update_task(field="depends_on", value="+id").

Params by action: create(source, target, type, note);
remove(source, target, type); query(source, target, type, depth);
validate(); reconcile(write) — reports stored links whose inverse is
missing, and adds those inverses only with write=True.
tools.name: backlog_link

tools.description:
Mark an existing handover as superseded by another.

Edits the old handover in place: prepends a SUPERSEDED callout, sets
`superseded_by: <new_id>` in its frontmatter. Use this to repair a
supersession chain after the fact (e.g., a handover was written without
`supersedes=`, but should chain off a prior one).

Both handovers must exist. Idempotent on the same `old_id` — calling it
again with a newer `new_id` updates the pointer instead of stacking
callouts.
tools.name: backlog_handover_supersede

tools.description:
Manually set a handover's status (open / closed / superseded).

Marks status_user_set: true — subsequent auto-transitions (supersession,
task-complete, resume) will skip this handover.
tools.name: backlog_handover_update_status

tools.description:
Log a systemic or recurring defect as a first-class Issue.

Issues require evidence of recurrence, systemic scope, or outstanding
customer impact — one-off defects should go to `backlog_bug_create` instead.
A *task* is the unit of work; an *issue* is the unit of broken-ness.
One issue can spawn multiple fix attempts; one task can close many issues.

body.description: Markdown body for repro steps + investigation notes.

components.description: Tags for which parts of the system are affected.

discovered_by.description: Who/what found it (manual QA, alert, customer report).

related_tasks.description: Task ids attempting or related to this issue.

severity.description: One of P0 (data loss/security), P1, P2, P3 (cosmetic).

tldr.description:
One-line essence of the issue. Auto-generated from impact or
title if omitted.

tools.name: backlog_issue_create

limit.description:
Max entries returned (default 50). 0 = no cap. An overflow footer
reports how many were hidden.

path.description:
Only issues whose `location` points under this path or matches
this glob; each row then shows the matching locations.

severity.description: Filter by severity: P0, P1, P2, P3.

status.description:
Filter by status: open, investigating, fixed, wontfix, duplicate,
or unresolved (open + investigating).

verbose.description:
If True, include body content (repro steps) per entry. Slim
(default) shows id, severity, status, title, and tldr.

tools.name: backlog_issue_list

tools.description:
Read issue <id>: slim frontmatter by default; verbose adds the body, sections picks named
sections (repro, investigation, notes), expand_links adds tldrs to linked ids.

sections.description: Named body sections to return instead of the slim view.

verbose.description: Include the full body (repro steps, investigation notes).

tools.name: backlog_issue_get

tools.description:
Set one field on an issue. List fields take a comma-separated value; an
empty value clears the field.

field ∈ {status, title, severity, impact, components, location,
related_tasks, fixed_in_task, duplicate_of, body}. Lifecycle: status=fixed
needs fixed_in_task (set it in a prior call), status=duplicate needs
duplicate_of; `resolved` auto-fills when status moves to fixed.
tools.name: backlog_issue_update

tools.description:
Import hand edits to issue files (an issue-only `backlog_sync`) and rebuild the issue index.

On a team server only the host operator can run it.
tools.name: backlog_issue_resync

tools.description:
Log a Bug — the user-flagged sink for defects that don't clear the Issue bar.

Bugs are project-wide lightweight artifacts (no aging window, no fix-by).
Use this for one-off defects, cosmetic issues, or anything the user wants
tracked but that doesn't yet meet the recurring/systemic/outstanding bar.

discovered_by.description:
'user' (default) when the user flagged the bug; 'claude' when you found it
and the user agreed to log it.

found_in.description: Optional task ID where the bug was flagged.

severity.description: Optional. P0|P1|P2|P3 if you want a sort hint.

tools.name: backlog_bug_create

tools.description:
Which bugs exist, filtered by status, the task they were found in, or the
code path they point at; the active set by default (and optionally archive).

Sorted by (status weight asc, discovered desc).

found_in.description: Filter by task ID where bug was discovered.

include_archive.description: If True, also include archived bugs.

limit.description:
Max entries returned (default 50). 0 = no cap. An overflow footer
reports how many were hidden.

path.description:
Only bugs whose `location` points under this path (a directory or
file, e.g. "pipeline/providers") or matches this glob ("viewer/*.js").
Each row then shows the matching locations.

status.description: Filter by status: open, fixed, shelved, adopted, promoted.

tools.name: backlog_bug_list

tools.description: Read a Bug. Falls through to archive if not in active set.

verbose.description: If True, return full frontmatter + body. Default is slim view.

tools.name: backlog_bug_get

tools.description:
Set one field on a Bug. List fields take a comma-separated value; an
empty value clears the field.

field ∈ {status, title, severity, components, location, fix_commit,
adopted_into, promoted_to, body}. Lifecycle (set the companion field first,
in a prior call): status=fixed needs fix_commit, status=adopted needs
adopted_into, status=promoted needs promoted_to.
tools.name: backlog_bug_update

tools.description:
Archive a fixed, adopted or promoted bug (refused while it is open or shelved).
Closing a task archives its fixed bugs already.
tools.name: backlog_bug_archive

tools.description:
Run the cross-bug signature scanner and return groups.

mode: "all" (default), "open_only", "end_of_task" (excludes archive).
Returns a human-readable digest of candidate groups; groups have >=2 bugs.

mode.description: Scan scope. "all" includes archive, "end_of_task" excludes it.

tools.name: backlog_bug_pattern_scan

tools.description:
Atomic: create an Issue from N Bugs; mark each Bug status=promoted.

The user must provide evidence_text — this is the systemic/recurring/
outstanding rationale that the new bar requires. Bugs are marked
promoted_to=<new ISS-NNN>.

body.description: Markdown body for the new Issue.

bug_ids.description: List of Bug IDs to promote (e.g. ["B-001", "B-002"]).

components.description: Component tags for the Issue. Inferred from bugs if omitted.

tools.name: backlog_bug_promote

tools.description:
Write a decision menu as a first-class entity (`DEC-NNN`).

Use when ≥2 mutually exclusive paths need user input. Replaces inline
option lists in chat — the decision survives the session.

raised_in.description: Optional handover id that surfaced this decision.

recommendation.description: 1-indexed pick from `options`. None if no preference.

task_id.description: Optional link to the task this decision blocks.

tools.name: backlog_decision_create

tools.description:
Read and transition existing decisions (DEC-NNN). To CREATE a decision use
backlog_decision_create. The taskmaster:decision skill presents the options to
the user and records the outcome.

Params by action: list(status — default "open"; "all" for every state —,
task_id, limit); get(decision_id);
resolve(decision_id, resolved_with, rationale, resolved_in);
drop(decision_id, reason); update(decision_id, title, options,
recommendation, body).
tools.name: backlog_decision

tools.description:
The viewer's continuity rail as JSON: open handovers, tasks, decisions,
issues and ideas, each with an `action_class` (review, decide, resume,
clean-up, ambient), most actionable first, capped at `limit`. For an agent's question
"what waits on a person" `backlog_list_tasks(waiting_on_human=True)` is the
direct answer.

Returns {"items": [...], "view", "total"}, plus "truncated": true when
`limit` cut the list.

limit.description: Max items (default 50); 0 returns every item in the rail's order.

tools.name: backlog_continuity_items

tools.description:
What changed in the backlog since a cursor, a time or an entity's creation, as JSON.

With no arguments it returns a cursor and nothing else ("start watching from now");
pass the cursor back to learn what moved. When a cursor can no longer be used,
the answer is not an error: `resync_required` is true, `reason` says why, and a
fresh cursor comes back. That is not a quiet period, so re-read what you care about.

Authored values are never returned. Each change names the fields that moved;
read the current value with `backlog_get_task` or `backlog_get_*`.

cursor.description: A cursor from an earlier call. Empty starts from now.

epic.description: Report only this epic and its tasks, including a task leaving it.

group_commits.description:
Group each transaction's changes into one commit entry. A legacy store
has no commit rows, so each change is its own commit there.

ids.description: Entity ids to report. Empty means all.

kinds.description: Entity kinds to report (task, bug, issue, ...). Empty means all.

limit.description: Commits (or changes, when ungrouped) per answer, 1-500.

since.description:
Start from a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp, or from an entity
id — "since handover X was written" is since="<X's id>": everything
after that entity was created. Instead of a cursor or since_seq. The
store's own import of existing files is left out, and counted in `note`.

since_seq.description: Start from this sequence instead of a cursor. 0 is all history.

tools.name: backlog_changes_since

tools.description:
What is in the way of a task — can it start, can it close today — and what
to know before working on it, as JSON, bounded by bytes.

One call in place of status + next_available + get_task + task_pipeline +
dependencies + bug and handover reads: `focus=<task id>, scope="task"`.
`mandatory` is what blocks the task: unsatisfied review gates, unmet or
unresolvable dependencies, open bugs filed against it, open handovers asking
for an action, a human action it waits on, and a live peer's claim. It is never
trimmed to fit: when the budget cannot hold it, `over_budget` is true,
`selected` is empty and the blockers still come back whole, so raise the
budget rather than trusting a short answer.

`clear` is true only when nothing blocks and every producer answered. One that
could not answer (an unreadable row, a dependency id that resolves to nothing,
no task in focus) appears as a blocker of kind `unknown`. `clear: false` means
something blocks or could not be checked; don't read it as clear. Tell the user
what blocks before you go on. Stop only for a peer's live claim, a human action in
review or a failed spec review; when the user asked for this task, report the
other blockers and proceed.

`selected` is the bounded convenience part, with a count of what was left out;
pass `cursor` back to continue it (no `cursor` means nothing remains).

budget_bytes.description: UTF-8 bytes the whole answer may use. Only selection is trimmed.

cursor.description: A cursor from an earlier call, to continue its selection.

focus.description: Task id. Empty takes the task this session picked, unless scope is project.

include.description:
Sections to select: spec, plan, body, links, handovers, bugs,
issues, notes, dependencies, siblings, recent. Omitted uses the scope's default; an empty list
returns blockers only.

scope.description: task, session or project — what the question is about.

tools.name: backlog_context

tools.description:
Log an idea — a lightweight, unvalidated thought. Lighter than a task.

An *idea* is a parking lot for things you might want to do, explore, or
revisit. It can grow into a task / issue later via linkage.
Title is required; everything else is optional. Status is freeform.

body.description: Markdown body — anything goes (sketches, code blocks, prose).

created_by.description:
Who logged it ("Claude" by default; "user" when
invoked via /add-idea).

related_issues.description: Issue ids this idea relates to.

related_tasks.description: Task ids this idea relates to.

tldr.description:
One-line essence of the idea. Auto-generated from body or
title if omitted.

tools.name: backlog_idea_create

tools.description:
List ideas, optionally filtered. With `idea_id`, returns one full record.

Without `idea_id`, returns slim one-liners (no body) — newest first. Pass
`verbose=True` to render the full record per entry (heavier payload). Output
caps at `limit` with an overflow footer (limit=0 for all). Filters compose as
AND. By default archived ideas are excluded.
tools.name: backlog_idea_list

tools.description:
Read idea <id>: slim frontmatter by default; verbose adds the body, expand_links adds tldrs to
linked ids. Ideas have no named sections, so `sections` returns an error.
tools.name: backlog_idea_get

tools.description:
Set one field on an idea. List fields take a comma-separated value; an
empty value clears the field.

field ∈ {title, body, status, tags, related_tasks, related_issues,
promoted_to, archived}. To promote an idea, set promoted_to then set
archived=true; archived takes true/false.
tools.name: backlog_idea_update

tools.description:
Manage sticky notes on the user's Desk: the lightest continuity surface, freeform and
not attached to tasks. For loose thoughts that fit no task, idea, issue or handover; one
consolidated note per session is usually enough. Leave user-authored notes as they are
unless the user asks you to change them.

Params by action: create(text, pinned); list(include_archived, limit);
get(note_id); update(note_id, text, pinned); archive(note_id).
tools.name: backlog_note

tools.description:
Create a new Area — a long-lived subsystem/workstream with NO status
lifecycle (e.g. "desktop-app", "viewer", "mcp-server").

Areas group epics and tasks by where they live in the codebase rather
than by when they finish — an area never completes or archives. If an
epic can say when it's done, it's an epic; if it can't, it's an area.
`anchors` is a list of path globs, or the same as a JSON array or a
comma-separated string.
tools.name: backlog_area_create

tools.description:
List all Areas — long-lived subsystems with no status lifecycle.

Returns one line per area: id, name, anchor count, first line of
description. Caps at `limit` (default 50; 0 = no cap) with an overflow
footer.
tools.name: backlog_area_list

tools.description:
What an Area is and what work is under it: its frontmatter and body, the
epics filed under it with their progress, and how many tasks it holds.
tools.name: backlog_area_get

tools.description: Update a single field on an Area.

field.description: Field to update — one of: name, description, anchors

value.description:
New value. For anchors: a list of path globs or a JSON array,
which REPLACES the whole list ("[]" clears it); or entries each
prefixed `+` (add) or `-` (remove), e.g. "+docs/viewer/**", which
edit it. A bare string is refused.

tools.name: backlog_area_update

tools.description: Return current viewer prefs as JSON.
tools.name: viewer_prefs_get

tools.description:
Deep-merge a JSON patch into the persisted viewer prefs.
Patch is a JSON object; only the keys present are updated.
tools.name: viewer_prefs_set

tools.description:
Create a new task under an epic. `phase` is required.

Common fields are top-level; rarely-set ones go in `options`. `tldr` is generated
from notes/title when omitted. `lane`, `component`, `design_change` and
`blast_radius_depth` are not create-time arguments; set them afterwards with
backlog_update_task.

bundle.description: Bundle slug (lowercase kebab, 2-41 chars) to group this task with its siblings.

depends_on.description: Comma-separated task ids that must be done first.

options.description:
Rarely-set fields as a dict: `docs` ("key:path;key:path", keys plan/spec/roadmap/design/analysis),
`sub_repo`, `stage` (int), `estimate` (S/M/L), `anchors` (comma-separated globs/URLs),
`task_id` (override the generated id), `area` (an existing Area id).
Other keys, and doc keys outside the list, are ignored.

tldr.description: One-line summary. Generated from notes/title when empty.

tools.name: backlog_add_task

tools.description:
Start working on a task — sets it to in-progress. Idempotent if already in-progress.

Picking takes a claim: the task is locked to this session until it completes,
the claim is released, or the claim expires. Keep a long task claimed with
`backlog_claim(action="renew")`, and give it back with `action="release"`.
On a shared server, a claim belongs to your session; your own earlier sessions that have
disconnected are taken over without force.

force.description:
Force-claim the task even if locked by another session. Use when a previous
   session ended without releasing the lock.

ttl_seconds.description:
How long this claim stands without a renew. 0 uses the default
   (4 hours). A claim also expires as soon as its holder is known to be gone.

tools.name: backlog_pick_task

tools.description:
Keep, give back or inspect the claim a pick took on a task, as JSON.

A claim is what stops two sessions working the same task. `backlog_pick_task`
takes one; this keeps it alive across a long session, hands it back when the
work pauses, and says who holds what.

A claim expires when its holder's process is known to be gone, or when its TTL
passes. A holder that cannot be judged — another machine, or a session this
store has never heard from — keeps its claim: the cost of guessing wrong is two
agents editing one task, so an unproven claim is never broken. `release` frees
an expired claim without stealing; `backlog_pick_task(force=True)` is still the
override for one that stands. On a shared server, a claim belongs to your session;
your own earlier sessions that have disconnected are taken over without force.

action.description: renew (extend to now + ttl), release (hand it back), status.

task_id.description: The task to act on. Omit with `status` to list this session's claims.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a renewed claim stands. 0 uses the default (4 hours).

tools.name: backlog_claim

tools.description:
Mark a task as done (or in-review) and optionally log a session summary to the PROGRESS.md changelog.

When session summary fields are provided, a changelog entry is appended automatically.
This combines the status transition and session logging into one atomic operation.

Use target_status="done" (default) when the work is complete and the gates passed.
Use "in-review" when only the human can unblock the task (API key, account access, a
config only they hold), and pass that as human_action.

Accepts tasks that are in-progress, in-review, or blocked.

auto_summary.description: If true, generates a lightweight auto-summary instead of the structured format. Pass git stats as the done field.

decisions.description: Optional newline-separated list of decisions made

done.description: Optional newline-separated list of accomplishments for the changelog

human_action.description: Required with target_status="in-review" (unless already set on the task): short imperative describing the human-only blocker, e.g. "add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env". Cleared automatically when the task reaches done.

issues.description: Optional newline-separated list of issues encountered. Use "None" if none.

patchnote.description: Optional 1-2 sentence user-facing release-note line describing what shipped. Leave empty for internal/infra tasks.

release.description: Optional release bucket this task ships in (e.g., "pre-alpha", "alpha-1.0"). Groups patchnotes for release notes.

session_title.description: Optional session title (e.g., "C++ Parser: Graph Analysis"). Auto-prefixed with today's date.

target_status.description: Target status — "done" (default) or "in-review" (blocked on a human-only action)

tasks_touched.description: Optional comma-separated task IDs that changed status this session

tools.name: backlog_complete_task

tools.description:
Archive a task — hides it from the board and default listings.
Tasks with status `done`, `blocked`, or `todo` can be archived. Archiving captures WHY the task
was archived (e.g., verified and done, deprecated, duplicate, won't fix).
Note: `todo` tasks require a reason other than "done" (e.g., deprecated, duplicate, wont-fix, superseded).

reason.description: Why the task is being archived. One of: done, deprecated, duplicate, wont-fix, superseded. Default: done.

tools.name: backlog_archive_task

tools.description:
What the last logged session did: the newest entry of the PROGRESS.md changelog (everything
between its first and second ### headings). Handovers are not read; when some are dated after
that entry the answer says how many and where to look.
tools.name: backlog_last_session

tools.description:
Update a single field on a task. Status changes trigger appropriate date updates.

Two calling styles are supported:
- Field/value style: backlog_update_task(task_id, field, value) — the classic API.
- Keyword style: backlog_update_task(task_id, tldr="...", next_step="...") — for tldr/next_step.

field.description:
Field to update, one of: title, status, priority, notes, branch, worktree, blockers,
docs, depends_on, sub_repo, stage, estimate, locked_by, review_instructions, phase,
anchors, area, lane, component, design_change, bundle, blast_radius_depth,
patchnote, release, tldr, next_step, human_action

next_step.description: Concrete immediate action to take on this task (keyword style only).

tldr.description: One-sentence essence of the task (keyword style only).

value.description:
New value. Format varies by field:
- status: todo, in-progress, in-review, done, blocked or archived (illegal transitions are
  refused; `in-review` needs human_action set first)
- priority: critical, high, medium or low
- notes: replaces the whole notes text (it does not append)
- docs: "key:path" with key one of plan, spec, roadmap, design, analysis
  (e.g., "plan:docs/plans/foo.md")
- depends_on: comma-separated task IDs (e.g., "cpp-parser-002,cpp-parser-003"),
  which replace the whole list; or ids each prefixed + or - ("+cpp-parser-004"),
  which add to or remove from it
- stage: integer
- estimate: size string (e.g., "S", "M", "L")
- sub_repo: sub-repo directory name for monorepo projects
- locked_by: refused — only backlog_pick_task and backlog_claim write a claim
- phase: phase ID to assign, or "" to clear
- anchors: comma-separated glob patterns/URLs, or "" to clear
- patchnote: 1-2 sentence user-facing release-note line, or "" to clear
- release: release bucket this task ships in (e.g., "pre-alpha", "alpha-1.0"), or "" to clear
- area: area id (must match an existing Area from `backlog_area_list`), or "" to clear
- lane: full, standard or express (which gates the task needs)
- component: a component declared on the task's epic, or "" to clear
- design_change: true or false, flagging a task that changes its epic's locked design
- bundle: bundle slug (lowercase kebab, 2-41 chars), or "" to clear
- blast_radius_depth: shallow or deep, or "" to clear
- human_action: what only the human can do; required before status in-review

tools.name: backlog_update_task

tools.description:
Record the outcome of a pipeline gate on a task (spec, plan, tests, impl, spec-review,
plan-review, design-review, review-gate). Status gates take status="done"; review gates
take a verdict in pass/warn/fail. Overwrites any prior record for that gate.

On a task with a lane, an earlier required gate must be satisfied (pass/done/skipped)
before a later one is recorded.

codex_used.description: True if the optional Codex adversarial pass was run.

commit_sha.description:
Full 40-character SHA of the commit the gate was run against (git rev-parse HEAD
in the task's worktree). The merge gate compares it exactly with the branch tip, so a
short SHA never matches.

spec_path.description: Path of the spec or plan that was reviewed, if any.

tools.name: backlog_record_gate

tools.description:
Stamp a merge rung on a task: records that the task's branch landed at `rung`
(e.g. develop|stage|master) at merge commit `sha`. Idempotent overwrite per rung.
The manual fallback for the PostToolUse merge-recorder hook. Not a pipeline gate —
no ordering is enforced; a rung label outside the ladder (e.g. "branch:<name>") is
still recorded to preserve the audit trail.

expect_commit.description: record only if the rung's current merge commit is this one ('' = none recorded); otherwise refused. Used by team-server hooks.

rung.description: Rung label (ladder label or "branch:<name>" for untracked targets).

tools.name: backlog_record_merge

tools.description:
Record an explicit, audited skip of a pipeline gate: the way past a required gate
without satisfying it. It always succeeds for a valid gate and reason, is recorded
with that reason, and is flagged on the dashboard.

gate.description: The gate to skip (see backlog_record_gate for valid names).

reason.description: Required non-empty justification (becomes the paper trail).

tools.name: backlog_skip_gate

tools.description: Remove a single gate record from a task and recompute gate_state.

gate.description: The gate to clear (see backlog_record_gate for valid names).

tools.name: backlog_clear_gate

tools.description:
Show a task's lane, its required gate pipeline, and each gate's recorded
state (pass/done/skipped/fail/pending), plus the one-line gate_state and the
list of outstanding gates blocking `done`. For everything else in the way
(dependencies, open bugs, handovers, a human action), use
`backlog_context(focus=<id>, scope="task")`.
tools.name: backlog_task_pipeline

tools.description: Alias of backlog_record_gate(gate="spec-review"); also keeps the legacy `spec_review` dict.

codex_used.description: True if the optional Codex adversarial pass was run

spec_path.description: Path to the spec/plan file that was reviewed

tools.name: backlog_set_spec_review

tools.description:
Alias of backlog_clear_gate(gate="spec-review"); also removes the legacy `spec_review` dict.
Use when the spec was revised and the prior review no longer applies.
tools.name: backlog_clear_spec_review

tools.description: Update a single field on an epic.

field.description: Field to update — one of: name, status, description, docs

value.description:
New value. For status, one of: active, planned, done.
For docs, use "key:path" format (e.g., "design:docs/design/foo.md").
Valid doc keys mirror task docs: plan, spec, roadmap, design, analysis.
Pass "key:" (empty path) to remove a single doc entry.

tools.name: backlog_update_epic

tools.description:
Archive an epic and all its tasks — hides the epic from the board and default listings.
Cascades: every non-archived task in the epic is also archived with the same reason.

reason.description: Why the epic is being archived. One of: done, deprecated, duplicate, wont-fix, superseded. Default: done.

tools.name: backlog_archive_epic

tools.description:
Create a new epic. Epics group related tasks into workstreams and are
strictly finite — every epic must say when it's done. If the work can't
say when it's done, it's an Area (see `backlog_area_create`), not an epic.

area.description:
Optional area id (e.g., "desktop-app") this epic lives under. Must
match an existing Area from `backlog_area_list`; leave empty if unset.

description.description: Brief description of the epic's scope and goals

done_when.description:
Required. The concrete condition under which this epic is complete
(e.g., "auth flow ships to prod with SSO + MFA"). Cannot be empty.

epic_id.description: Short kebab-case identifier (e.g., "auth-system", "perf-opt"). Must be unique. Used as prefix for task IDs.

status.description: Initial status — one of: active, planned (default: planned)

tools.name: backlog_add_epic

tools.description:
Create a new phase. Phases are temporal attention scopes for sequential ordering, NOT feature
groupings — features belong in epics. Only one phase is active at a time; tasks are assigned
to phases to control focus.

description.description: Brief description of the phase's goals

order.description: Position in the sequence (1, 2, 3...). Auto-assigned if omitted.

phase_id.description: Short kebab-case identifier (e.g., "foundation", "mvp", "polish"). Must be unique. Avoid "p1"/"p2" — too similar to priority names.

start_date.description: Optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD format). Auto-set to today if status is active and omitted.

tools.name: backlog_add_phase

tools.description: Update a single field on a phase.

field.description: Field to update — one of: name, status, description, order, target_date, start_date

value.description: New value. For status: planned, active, done, archived. For order: integer. For dates: YYYY-MM-DD or empty to clear.

tools.name: backlog_update_phase

tools.description: Show detailed progress for a phase. Defaults to the active phase.

phase_id.description: Phase ID. If omitted, shows the active phase.

tools.name: backlog_phase_status

tools.description:
Show progress for an epic: status counts, per-component rollup, and the
design-maturity lock. Derived on read from the epic's tasks — no stored rollup.
tools.name: backlog_epic_status

tools.description:
Complete the active phase and activate the next one in sequence.
Archives all 'done' tasks in the completed phase. Activates the next 'planned' phase by order.
Refuses while the phase has unchecked deliverables or tasks that are not done, unless force=True.

force.description:
If True, advance anyway: the phase is marked done and its unfinished
tasks keep their status.

tools.name: backlog_advance_phase

tools.description:
Apply multiple task/epic updates in one call. Two forms; pass exactly one.

Use this instead of calling backlog_update_task repeatedly — it's faster and atomic.

atomic.description:
Only for the `commands` form, which is all-or-nothing; pass True to
say so explicitly. The line form's partial apply cannot be made atomic.

commands.description:
Typed mutations — [{"operation": "task.patch", "arguments": {...}}]
— applied in ONE transaction, all of them or none. Each operation is
validated by name against the store's operation allowlist; there is no
passthrough. Native-authority stores only. Answered as JSON.

expected_revisions.description:
[{"kind", "id", "revision"}] preconditions for the
`commands` form. A mismatch applies nothing and says so.

operations.description:
Newline-separated list of operations. Each line format:
"update {task_id} {field} {value}" — update a task field
"status {task_id} {new_status}" — shorthand for status changes
"complete {task_id}" — mark task done (shorthand for status done)
"archive {task_id} [reason]" — archive a task (default reason: done)
"pick {task_id}" — set task to in-progress with started timestamp
"update_epic {epic_id} {field} {value}" — update an epic field
This form is partial: a bad line reports its own error and every good
line still applies. Answered as text.

tools.name: backlog_batch_update

tools.description: Preview what a batch of task operations would do without writing to disk.

operations.description:
Newline-separated list of operations to preview. Each line is:
"complete {task_id}" — preview marking a task as done
"archive {task_id}" — preview archiving a task
"pick {task_id}" — preview picking a task
"status {task_id} {new_status}" — preview a status change

tools.name: backlog_batch_preview

tools.description:
Analyze the blast radius (impact footprint) of a task.

Two modes:
- predictive: metadata-only analysis for pick-task time. Fast, no code tracing.
- evidence: code-level impact analysis for review-gate time. Traces imports, builds dependency graph.

depth_override.description: Optional depth override — "shallow" (0-1 hop) or "deep" (2 hops). Overrides the adaptive heuristic.

structured.description: When True and mode is "predictive", return the raw analysis as a JSON string instead of formatted markdown. Used for detection-fallback pipelines.

tools.name: backlog_blast_radius

tools.description: Open the backlog kanban board in the default browser. The viewer auto-loads current data.
tools.name: backlog_open_viewer

tools.description:
Return the full .taskmaster/project.yaml as a dict, or None if missing/invalid.

The returned dict is the EXPANDED form — every dataclass default is filled
in (e.g. `project.goal == ""` even when the YAML didn't set it). For "is
this field absent in the source?" queries, use `backlog_project_get_field`
which reads the raw YAML.
tools.name: backlog_project_get

tools.description:
Read a single field via dotted/indexed path from the RAW YAML.

Unlike `backlog_project_get`, this reads the source file directly without
coercing through dataclasses — so absent fields return None rather than
their schema defaults. Examples:
    "meta.name"
    "repos[0].name"
    "repos[0].branches.protected[0]"

Returns None if any segment is missing or out of range.
tools.name: backlog_project_get_field

tools.description:
Return repos in topological dependency order. Empty list if no manifest.

Raises ValueError if depends_on contains a cycle (caught by validator on load).
tools.name: backlog_project_ship_order

tools.description:
Write .taskmaster/project.yaml with strict validation.

Raises ValueError if YAML is malformed or schema invalid. The manifest is
a store-owned entity, so the write commits through a store transaction.
Returns the absolute path written, followed by the committed `[seq N]`.
tools.name: backlog_project_set

tools.description:
Scaffold a minimal valid project.yaml. Refuses to overwrite.

Returns a confirmation message including the path written, followed by the
committed `[seq N]`.
tools.name: backlog_project_init

tools.description:
Return the observability error-trace ladder as a list of dicts.

Empty list if no manifest.
tools.name: backlog_project_error_trace_ladder

tools.description:
Drive Taskmaster's Linear sync. First-time setup is probe (lists teams and statuses), then
bootstrap_apply with the status/priority mapping the user approved; the taskmaster:linear
skill walks through it.

Params by action: probe(token_env); bootstrap_apply(workspace_alias, team_id,
token_env, status_mapping, priority_mapping, default_workspace);
link(task_id, external_key, workspace_alias); unlink(task_id); list();
show(tracker_id); status(); retry(target_id, request_id, caller_scope).
Native retry returns its request_id/caller_scope; retain both and the target
to inspect a pending result or recover a lost response without a new push.
tools.name: backlog_linear
